note: Twenty-five pages at 612x792 pt except the newspaper page 23 at 595.32x841.92, forty-six measured regions and fifteen exhibits: Figures 1-11, a captioned photograph with no number on the newspaper page, and three table rows. Six table numbers print but only three own a drawn region, because Tables 2, 5 and 6 draw their rules as per-column segments. Eleven figures are cited by ASCII "Figure N" pointers and four of them are never cited at all. Families from the pixels: line 3, composite-panel 2, flowchart-or-schematic 4, node-link-network 2, heatmap-or-contour 1, photo-or-raster-image 1, table-grid 3.
rules: Six table numbers print and only three of them own a drawn region. Tables 2, 5 and 6 draw each booktabs rule as a run of per-column segments rather than one page-wide stroke - the widest segment in the paper is 98.9 pt against the 306 pt half-page bar the rule detector needs - so no rule qualifies, the segments are dropped as dividers, and the census carries three table-grid rows against six printed numbers. Tables 2 and 6 print below their captions at the foot of the page, Table 5 in the middle of p18. [caption.numbering] is "Table N:" on the three recorded rows.

The measured region of Table 1 stops eight points short of its last two rows: the box ends at y 168.4 while descriptions still print at 173.4 and 191.4, with the vector symbols for those rows at y 174.9-203.2 falling outside it. The row count in [table.rows] is the printed count - one header row and six notation rows, 18 pt pitch - not the four the bounding box encloses. Table 1 also prints only two horizontal rules, the caption-to-header and header-to-body rules, with no closing rule under the last row.

Caption side is a two-group decision with no exceptions: all eleven figure captions print BELOW their art at 8.0-10.6 pt and all three recorded table captions print ABOVE at 0.4-9.2 pt of clearance. The captions are short noun phrases - the longest is fourteen words - and none states a unit, a variable count, a condition or a conclusion, so [caption.position] carries the whole side signal and the offset only confirms it. Two of them are not their own text line: the extractor prints Figure 2's caption split across two lines in reverse order, the tail line above the head line, which is why that caption is recorded as typed rather than sliced.

Six exhibits sit under the heading of the section that follows them, so the section attribution has to be read from the printed heading order rather than taken from the nearest heading: Table 1 prints on p5 above the section 4 heading and belongs to section 3 Notation, the heading it follows on p4; Table 3 prints on p15 above the 6.3 heading at y 573.9 and belongs to 6.2.5; Table 4 and Figure 7 print on p17 above the section 7 heading at y 614.9 and belong to 6.3.3; Figure 10 prints on p21 above the section 8 heading at y 435.7 and belongs to 7.4; Figure 11 prints on p22 above the section 9 heading at y 271.8 and belongs to section 8. Figure 1 and Figure 6 are the mirror case, attached by the context pass to the heading below them, 3 Notation and 6.2.2, when they belong to 1.3 Our Work and 6.2. [place.section_path] records the corrected path on those eight rows and the context dump's own path on the other seven.

Every pointer is ASCII: "Figure N" eleven times and "Table N" five times, with no ligature abbreviation, no "Fig." and no parenthetical form, so the ligature hazard that hides pointers in other papers in this block does not bite here. The panel pointers carry the sub-label, "Figure 8(a)", "Figure 9(b)" and so on, and one of them prints with no space - "Figure8(b)" on p18 - so a scan for "Figure " plus a digit misses it. [mention.style] keeps both spellings as printed.

Four numbered exhibits are never cited by number: Figures 1, 6 and 10 and Table 4 print no body pointer at all, their caption line being their only occurrence, and Table 4 is instead introduced as "as shown in Table." with the number dropped. [mention.count] is 0 on those four rows and [mention.first_page] is null; the pattern field is "none" there rather than a guess. A census that counted only numbered pointers would report eleven cited exhibits and miss the four that are not, and it would also lose the four whose citation arrives one page early - Figure 9 is cited on p19 and printed on p20, Figure 11 on p21 and p22 - which is what [mention.lead_pages] records.

Five of the eleven figures are two-panel rasters and each panel is a separate embedded image with its own frame and its own in-axes legend, not one image split by the pass, so the recorded bbox is one panel wide while [geometry.panel_count] is 2. Figure 9 is the exception with three panels: its (a) is itself a two-high stack of a convergence scatter over a four-bar chart, with the Value-Cost grid of (b) beside it. The left panel is recorded and the rest excluded as fragments, which keeps the region count honest without pretending the caption covers one plot.

Rule style is not uniform here. Table 4 is a three-rule booktabs table, four columns by three body rows with the Value/Level and Cost/Level header pair on one line. Table 3 is a full grid - twelve horizontal rules and six vertical ones, a boxed frame, one merged first column spanning the whole table and shaded header cells - so [table.rule_style] is "boxed" there and "booktabs" on Table 4. Table 1 is booktabs with the closing rule omitted. No cell fill, banding or vertical rule appears anywhere except in Table 3.

Page 23 is a different sheet and a different species of page: 595.32x841.92 pt against the 612x792 of the other twenty-four, laid out two columns with a headline in display type, decorative foliage behind the text and a forest-scene band across the foot, and it carries the only uncaptioned photograph in the file. The photograph is recorded as an exhibit - it is content, not furniture - while the foliage, the stump clip art and the foot band are excluded as background. [geometry.family] is photo-or-raster-image on that row and the three appendix-style decorations are not mistaken for it.

The twenty-two remaining vector regions are displayed equations: nineteen carry a parenthesised number from (1) to (31) with gaps, two are unnumbered inline expressions set as their own box, and one - on p16 - holds the axis bounds in the middle of a sentence. They are excluded as not-an-exhibit rather than recorded, since they print no caption and no figure number: [caption.verbatim] is empty on all of them and [mention.count] is 0, and no region is recorded as an item for the same reason. Sampling every fourth region would have opened eleven equation boxes and five real exhibits.

Nothing here is numbered for the reader: there is no running head, no folio and no watermark on any interior page, so a page-level cross-check cannot use a printed page number the way it can in papers whose headers carry one. Page 1 is the contest control sheet ("Problem Chosen E 2022"), pages 24 and 25 are the reference list, and neither carries a measured region, so [place.solo_page] is false on all forty-six regions and the census cannot lean on page isolation to separate exhibits from prose.
